title: Giant Dino Footprints Found — A T. rex Took a Stroll!
summary:
Imagine walking along and finding footprints as big as a bathtub. That's what happened in North Dakota! Scientists found four giant footprints left by an adult T. rex. This is super rare because dinosaur footprints usually don't last. But these did, for about 66.5 million years!

The footprints are each about three feet long. That's as long as a yardstick! The T. rex that made them was probably a big adult. It walked at about 3.5 to 4.5 miles per hour. That's like a person power-walking. So this T. rex wasn't in a hurry. It was just strolling around.

Scientists found the footprints on federal land near Marmath, North Dakota. They used a special 3D scanner to make digital copies. They even made physical copies you can touch.

Why are footprints so cool? Because they show what the dinosaur was doing. Bones tell us what the animal looked like, but footprints show us how it moved. Tyler Lyson, a scientist at the Denver Museum of Nature & Science, said, "With a trackway, we can actually follow an animal as it moved across the landscape."

Later this year, scientists plan to dig up three of the footprints and fly them by helicopter to the Denver Museum. Then you might get to see them in person! This is the first time we have a path made by an adult T. rex. How awesome is that?
why_it_matters: This discovery shows that even something as simple as a footprint can help scientists learn about Earth's history, and soon you may be able to see these tracks at a museum.

background_read: T. rex (short for Tyrannosaurus rex, one of the biggest meat-eating dinosaurs that ever lived) roamed Earth millions of years ago.
Usually, animal footprints wash away or crumble, so they are preserved only if mud or sand hardens in just the right way.
These prints were found in North Dakota (a U.S. state), and the Denver Museum of Nature & Science (a big science museum in Colorado) plans to put real tracks and touchable copies on display.
Article_Structure: WHO: Tyler Lyson, a scientist at the Denver Museum of Nature & Science, and other scientists.
WHAT: Four giant footprints from an adult T. rex were discovered, each about three feet long.
WHERE: On federal land near Marmath, North Dakota.
WHY: Footprints show how a T. rex actually moved, and this is the first path made by an adult T. rex scientists have found.

perspectives.perspective: The scientists who made the discovery
perspectives.description: They are excited because a set of footprints lets them follow how the T. rex moved instead of just seeing what its bones looked like.
They can use the digital copies to study the footprints too, without touching or damaging the real ones.
They will get to see real dinosaur footprints up close, and the physical copies can be touched by everyone.
